_comment: Incident-response playbook knowledge base. Each playbook maps to one or more ATT&CK techniques and provides ordered analyst actions. suggest_playbook() matches on technique id or free-text keywords.

playbooks.name: Reconnaissance / Scanning Response
steps: Confirm the scan source and scope from firewall/IDS logs.
Determine whether any scanned service responded or exposed a banner.
Rate-limit or block the source at the perimeter if it has no business need.
Check threat intel for the source IP/ASN reputation.
Watch for follow-on exploitation against the scanned services over the next 24h.

playbooks.name: Credential Attack Response
steps: Identify targeted accounts and whether any authentication succeeded.
Block the source IP if it is external and has no business justification.
Force-reset credentials for any account with a successful or near-miss auth.
Enforce/verify MFA on affected accounts.
Review authentication logs for the last 72h for lateral movement or impossible-travel logins.
If a service account is involved, rotate its secret and audit its usage.

playbooks.name: Web Exploitation Response
steps: Identify the targeted endpoint and payload class from web/WAF logs.
Confirm whether the WAF blocked the request or it reached the application.
Check application/database logs for evidence of successful injection or data return.
Patch or virtual-patch the vulnerable component; confirm affected versions against CVE data.
If data access is confirmed, initiate the data-breach process and preserve evidence.

playbooks.name: Malware / C2 Response
steps: Isolate the affected endpoint(s) from the network immediately.
Capture volatile evidence (memory, running processes, network connections) before reimaging.
Extract and pivot on the file hash and C2 IP/domain across the estate.
Block the C2 indicators at DNS/proxy/firewall.
Scope lateral movement and identify patient zero.
Reimage from a known-good baseline; rotate any credentials used on the host.

playbooks.name: Phishing Response
steps: Pull the message from all recipient mailboxes (purge).
Identify who received, opened, and clicked; prioritise clickers.
Reset credentials for any user who submitted credentials to the lure page.
Block the sender domain/URL at the mail gateway and web proxy.
Report the indicators to threat intel and check for reuse across incidents.
